title: Injection of Porcine Adipose Tissue-Derived Stroma Cells via Waterjet Technology
protocol: Use porcine adipose tissue from the Institute for Experimental Surgery in a sterile bench.
Mince the tissue into small fragments and mush using two scalpels (No. 10).
Transfer minced tissue into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Incubate with 5 ml of homogenizer solution for 30 min at 37°C on a shaker.
Stop incubation by adding 10 ml of growth media to the mixture.
Incubate the centrifuge tubes for 10 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the fraction with adipocytes from the top layer of the liquid and discard it.
Filter the remaining stromal fraction through a 100 µm cell sieve with a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) membrane to retrieve only the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the filtered cell suspension for 7 min at 630 x g at room temperature.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of PBS to wash the cells once.
Centrifuge the cell suspension again for 7 min at 630 x g at room temperature.
After centrifugation, resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of growth media per flask and seed cells in 75 cm² cell culture flasks.
Wash cells with 10 mL of PBS twice when they reach 70% confluence.
Aspirate PBS completely to remove remaining growth media.
Add 3 mL of 0.05%-Trypsin-EDTA per flask to detach the cells.
Incubate flasks for 3 min at 37 °C.
Check under the microscope if cells are detached.
If necessary, incubate flasks for up to 5 min at 37 °C.
Add 3 mL of growth media to stop the trypsinization process.
Transfer the detached cells to a centrifugation tube.
Centrifuge for 7 min at 630 x g at room temperature.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL of growth media.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Seed cells with an inoculation density of 3 x 10^5 cells per 75 cm² flask.
Wash cells twice with 10 mL of PBS.
Add 5 mL of dye solution per 75 cm² flask.
The dye solution consists of growth media with 2 µM green-fluorescent membrane-permeable live-cell dye and 4 µM red-fluorescent membrane-impermeant viability indicator.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature in the dark.
Aspirate and discard the dye solution.
Wash cells again twice with 10 mL of PBS.
Add growth media.
Document green and red fluorescence signal by fluorescence microscopy.
Place the 75 cm² flask on the microscope table.
Use the 10x objective for imaging.
Select no fluorescence filter.
Activate the transmitted light path.
Open the software program.
Press the Live button under the Locate tab to obtain a live image of the cells in the flask and focus on them using coarse and fine adjustment drives.
Apply a checkmark for Auto Exposure in the Camera sub-tab.
Take the first picture with transmitted light by pressing Snap.
Insert the scale bar using the Graphics tab and selecting Scale Bar.
Save the image using the Files tab and selecting Save as czi.
Change the filter to the one specific for green or red fluorescence manually on the microscope.
Select the reflected light path manually.
Press the Live button under the Locate tab again to obtain a live image of the cells with either green or red fluorescence.
Take the second picture with either green or red fluorescence by pressing Snap.
Insert the scale bar using the Graphics tab and selecting Scale Bar.
Dissect the urethra and the connecting bladder out of the pig.
Transport the dissected tissue on wet ice to the laboratory.
Place the urethra with the bladder on a sponge.
Use the bladder to determine the orientation (proximal, distal, dorsal, and ventral) of the urethra.
Cut open the urethra longitudinally on the dorsal side with aid of a catheter.
Inject cells into the opened urethra as described in subsequent chapters.
Label cells with a green-fluorescent membrane-permeable live-cell dye.
Aspirate the cell suspension using a syringe.
Apply the Williams cystoscopic injection needle (WN) to the aspirated cell suspension.
Hold the needle shortly above 2 mL of growth media in a 15 mL centrifugation tube or insert it into the opened urethra tissue.
Inject 250 µL of cells manually.
Collect cells injected into media directly by centrifuging for 7 min at 630 x g at room temperature.
For cells injected into the cadaveric urethra, aspirate them out of the injection dome with an 18G needle applied on a syringe.
Transfer the injected and aspirated cells into a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the transferred cells for 7 min at 630 x g at room temperature.
Resuspend the cells in 4 mL of growth media after centrifugation.
Mix 20 µL of cell suspension thoroughly with 20 µL of Trypan blue.
Fill 10 µL of this mixture into each chamber of the hemocytometer.
Count cells in all four corner squares under a microscope for both chambers.
Harvest cells as described in step 2.
Adjust cell density for injections to 6 x 10^6 cells per mL.
Fill the cell suspension into the dosing unit of the WJ device.
Inject 100 μL of cells by the device using a high pressure for tissue penetration followed by a low-pressure phase for cell injections.
Collect cells injected into media directly by centrifugation for 7 min at 630 x g at room temperature.
Aspirate cells out of the injection dome with an 18G needle applied on a syringe.
Transfer the injected and aspirated cells into a centrifugation tube.
Centrifuge the transferred cells for 7 min at 630 x g at room temperature.
Resuspend cells in 4 mL of growth media after centrifugation.
Determine cell yield and viability using Trypan blue dye exclusion with a hemocytometer.
Seed cells in tissue culture dishes at a density of 5 x 10^5 cells per dish.
Incubate the seeded cells for 3 h at 37 °C.
Replace growth media with 3 mL of Leibovitz's L-15 media without L-glutamine before AFM measurement.
Place the tissue culture dish in the sample holder of the AFM device.
Turn on the Petri dish heater set to 37 °C for the sample holder.
Use a glass block specified for liquid measurements and adjust it on the AFM holder.
Carefully place the cantilever on the surface of the glass block.
Ensure tip A lays over the polished optical plane.
Add a metallic spring with tweezers to stabilize the cantilever on the glass block.
Place the glass block with the spring on the AFM head and lock the integrated locking mechanism.
Mount the AFM head on the AFM device, ensuring the spring faces the left side.
Initialize the software setup and open the laser alignment window and approach parameter settings.
Turn on the stepper motor, the laser light, and the CCD-camera.
Identify the cantilever tip A using the CCD-camera.
Lower the cantilever until it is fully dipped into the medium using the stepper motor function.
Align the laser on top of the cantilever by adjusting the screws to ensure the reflected beam falls onto the center of the photodetector and the sum of the signals reaches 1 V or higher.
Ensure lateral and vertical deflections are close to 0.
Monitor the center in the laser alignment function and signal values.
Adjust further if signal values are incorrect.
Run the scanner Approach with specified parameters (Table 1).
Retract the cantilever by 100 µm once it reaches the bottom.
Ensure no cell is attached at the approach field.
Set up Run parameters: Setpoint 1 V, Pulling Length 90 µm, Velocity 5 µm/s, Sample rate 2000 Hz and Delay Mode Constant Force.
Start calibration force-distance curve measuring by pressing the button Run.
Select the region of linear fit in the software on the obtained calibration force-distance curve.
Calculate spring constant measurement by the software.
Calibrate cantilever following Danalache et al. parameters and steps.
Visually identify a cell and focus on it.
Place computer mouse at the middle of the cell.
Position AFM tip directly above the cell nucleus for precise measurements.
Focus on the cantilever and move it on the computer mouse.
Start the measurement with the parameters given in Table 2.
Measure at least 50 cells, each cell measured three times.
Process the data following exact steps and parameters as previously described by Danalache17.
Save and export the file.
Open the statistical software.
Choose New Dataset from the selection menu.
Select the DataSet file.
Open the Variable View tab.
Insert numeric variables for site injection (capture fluid or cadaveric tissue), category (control, WJ injection, WN injection) and elasticity.
Insert measured elasticity data with their corresponding site injection and category number in the Data View tab.
Analyze the data by selecting Analyze | Descriptive Statistics and choosing Exploratory data analysis.
Select Elasticity as the dependent variable and Category as the factor list.
Perform a statistical test by selecting Independent Samples within Nonparametric Test under the menu bar tab Analyze.
Keep settings in the tab Objective and Settings.
Open the tab Fields and choose Elasticity as Test Fields and Category as Groups.
Press Run.
